critical_code_review_comments: useSharedMicStream.js singleton: acquireSharedMic correctly serialises concurrent callers via a shared `_pending` Promise — no race where two callers each grab their own getUserMedia. The `_pending = null` cleanup happens in finally{}; the post-await `if (s) _refcount += 1` guard correctly avoids bumping the refcount on a failed acquire. releaseSharedMic clamps the floor at 0 and stops tracks only when the LAST consumer releases — exactly the WebRTC best-practice.

PushToTalkButton.ensureStream has a subtle but correct refcount-drift guard: heldRef.current tracks whether THIS component holds a ref; if a 2nd ensureStream() call happens (e.g. retry after permission flap), it immediately releaseSharedMic() to keep the PTT-side refcount==1. Without this, repeated presses could leak refs and prevent track teardown.

AVSeats.joinCall sequence (acquireSharedMic → getUserMedia({video}) → composeAVStream) cleanly decouples the two device acquisitions — mic LED stays off if the user disables video too, since the audio track is only held while acquireSharedMic refcount > 0. Video tracks are owned by AVSeats and must be stopped separately (noted in the lifecycle comments).

voice_lines.py L93 projection fix is correct & matches the storage schema (characters.owner_id, not user_id). The L101 ownership check `char.get('owner_id') != user['id']` now matches the projection. Without this fix, every player-side PTT 403'd silently — a real latent bug.
bestiary.py _color_for thresholds (<1, <5, <11, <17, ≥17) map cleanly to landing-page palette tiers. NaN/None handling via try/except + fallback to 1 (gold tier) is sensible.
bestiary.py id-namespacing (dnd5e: / anime5e: / cypher: / custom:) avoids collisions when systems share monster names (e.g. 'goblin') — keeps spawn determinism if a campaign later flips system_id.

BattlemapSidebar bestiary spawn testid uses the raw bestiary row id which already contains a colon (e.g. 'dnd5e:goblin') — fine for Playwright since attribute selectors handle colons, but consumers parsing the testid suffix downstream should anticipate the prefix:slug shape.

gm_voice.py lazy-create correctly checks `find_one({campaign_id, is_gm_voice:True})` before insert — idempotent at the data layer. The auth gate `(admin OR gm_id OR in member_ids)` matches the documented contract; 404 takes precedence over 403 because the campaign lookup happens first.
